title: Interaction-induced period shift of the Kohn oscillation in a parity-time-symmetric harmonic trap
abstract: The center of mass of a Bose--Einstein condensate in a harmonic trap oscillates at the trap frequency independently of the interactions. Without interactions a parity-time-symmetric gain-loss gradient leaves this frequency unchanged, and a cloud of the ground-state width is translated rigidly while the atom number is periodically modulated. With interactions the protection is lost, because the gain and the loss change the number of atoms; the modulated atom number drives the width of the cloud, and the width acts back on the center of mass. At small gain the period grows quadratically with the gain strength, with a coefficient that in the Thomas--Fermi regime is set by the size of the cloud alone. The family of periodic orbits continued from the Kohn oscillation can be followed up to a critical gain, where it comes into resonance with highly excited states of the trap, and over the computed families this critical gain decreases with the amplitude of the oscillation and with the size of the cloud. A five-variable moment model reproduces the period and the width of the cloud along the orbits nearly up to the critical gain.
summary: This paper analyzes the period shift of the Kohn oscillation in a Bose-Einstein condensate trapped in a harmonic potential modified by gain and loss (PT-symmetry). The authors show that interactions cause the oscillation period to deviate from the non-interacting value, predicting the shift scales quadratically with gain at small strengths. They use advanced numerical methods to track these periodic orbits up to resonance points.
main_problem: The study investigates how interatomic interactions modify the period of the Kohn oscillation in a Bose-Einstein condensate confined in a harmonic trap subjected to a parity-time-symmetric gain-loss potential.
main_result: The period shift is found to be non-zero and proportional to the square of the gain strength ($\gamma^2$) at small gains, and the analysis determines scaling exponents for the critical gain where resonance occurs.
method: The research employs the Gross-Pitaevskii equation, utilizing moment models, Ehrenfest theorems, and advanced numerical techniques like pseudo-arclength continuation to track periodic orbits.
model_or_system: The system is a Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) governed by a GP equation incorporating a harmonic trap, repulsive interactions ($g|\psi|^2$), and a gain-loss term ($\propto \gamma x$), making the potential PT-symmetric.
key_observables: Period of oscillation ($T$), cloud width, center of mass position ($X(t)$), and the critical gain ($\gamma_c$) where resonance occurs.
important_parameters: Interaction strength ($g$), gain strength ($\gamma$), trap frequency ($\omega$), and the initial ground-state width ($\sigma_0$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on approximations such as fixed profile shape in the moment model, and the use of continuation methods near resonance points.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the time evolution of density and COM position for $\gamma=0$, show the period $T$ vs. $\gamma$ confirming quadratic growth, and compare results from different numerical domains/tapering schemes.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from the linear (non-interacting) case to the interacting case, deriving analytical approximations for small gain, developing moment equations, and finally using advanced numerical continuation techniques to map out the periodic orbits up to critical resonance points.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses non-Hermitian physics in the context of ultracold atoms, showing how gain/loss terms fundamentally alter coherent dynamics like the Kohn oscillation, which is crucial for understanding open quantum systems in atomic traps.
